**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off **Issue:** Removing `escapeHtml` and feeding `body` straight into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` turns every comment into executable HTML. A body like `` or `` runs in the browser of anyone who views the comment. **Failure mode:** Any user-controlled or attacker-influenced `body` gets full DOM XSS in the viewer’s origin (session theft, UI rewrite, drive-by actions as the victim). **Fix:** Do not assign raw `body` to `__html`. Either (1) render plain text / structured React nodes from a markdown parser with an allowlist, or (2) sanitize with a library such as DOMPurify before `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Restoring `escapeHtml` alone restores safety but drops rich formatting — pair escaping/sanitization with a real formatter if bold/links are required. ```suggestion return
{body}
; ``` (If rich HTML is required, replace the suggestion with sanitization + allowlisted tags rather than raw `body`.)

summary: ## Verdict **Critical XSS regression** — do not merge until comment HTML is sanitized or rendered safely. ## What went wrong `Comment` previously escaped `&`, `<`, and `>` before injecting into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, which made user/comment text safe as plain text. This PR deletes `escapeHtml` and passes `body` through raw. Any comment author (or anyone who can influence `body`) can inject script, event handlers, or malicious links that run in every viewer’s session. There is no markdown parser and no HTML sanitizer in the tree — the change does not implement “bold/links”; it implements arbitrary HTML execution. ## Fix direction - Prefer React text/`markdown-to-react` with an allowlist (e.g. bold/italic/links only), **or** - Keep `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` only after a well-tested sanitizer (DOMPurify or equivalent) with a strict allowlist. - Add a regression test: `` and `
